Ryasnopil Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ryasnopil, Ukraine

Demolished. This cemetery's founding is undocumented, though it appears on a 1917 Russian topographic map; per local residents, it was demolished in the 1980s. A local legend claims those who demolished the site were cursed and died of cancer; a neighbor who recently found one surviving gravestone reportedly reburied it out of fear of the curse rather than keep it. Per local historian V. Labunsky, the son of Ryasnopil landlord Gnat Gizhitsky invited Galician Jews to settle permanently in the 1820s, helping the village become an Odesa uyezd trade center; the community built a residential quarter with workshops, shops, and a synagogue. Population reached 105 (25%) by 1881. During a March-April 1919 pogrom, Jews fought back against an attack by the Grigoriev unit. The community's fate during the Holocaust is unknown.
